idea: Skip UP (yes) bets when BTC is down more than 1.5% over the last 6 hours.
evidence: regime-study 2026-11-20: across 12.6k rounds, buying UP at the ask after a >1.5% 6-h drop returned about -5c a contract against about -2.5c in other rounds, same sign in both halves of the data, but only 41-52 distinct days, not monotone (>3% drops showed nothing) and one of many cuts tried. Multi-day trends (24 h, 7 d, distance below the 7-d high) showed no consistent mispricing.
pass_rule: Judged only on rounds after the registration date. Market-wide: UP-at-ask result in tagged rounds at least 2c worse than in other rounds, more than 2 standard errors apart, with 200+ tagged rounds (about 25+ distinct days). Bot: tagged UP fills net negative with 30+ fills. Both must hold before it is proposed for the paper bot; real orders only on the owner's yes.
kill_rule: Market-wide difference within 1c of zero after 300 tagged rounds.

idea: The bot's bets against the 6-hour trend (UP when BTC is down more than 0.5% over 6 h, DOWN when up more than 0.5%) do worse than its bets with the trend.
evidence: journal 2026-11-20, in-sample: paper against-trend fills -6.1c +/- 4.4 a contract (n 93) vs with-trend +4.6c +/- 3.2 (n 139), about 2 standard errors apart; live the same direction on 13 vs 18 fills. Market-wide the 6-h trend is priced in (regime study), so if real this is the bot's model (no momentum) overstating its edge against the trend, not Kalshi mispricing it.
pass_rule: Judged only on bot fills (paper + live) after the registration date: against-trend fills at least 3c a contract worse than with-trend fills, more than 2 standard errors apart, with 80+ against-trend fills. Then proposed as a paper-only filter; real orders only on the owner's yes.
kill_rule: Difference within 1c of zero, or with-trend fills worse, after 120 against-trend fills.
